p.src: Little by little, I learned the everyday language used by the kappa. Consequently, I also began to understand the customs and habits of the kappa. The strangest of these was their absurd habit of finding amusing what we human beings take seriously, while taking seriously what we human beings find amusing. For example, we human beings take such things as justice and humanity seriously; but when the kappa hear of them, they clutch their bellies and burst out laughing. In short, their standard for what constitutes the ridiculous must be entirely different from ours. Once I was discussing birth control with Chuck, the doctor. At that, Chuck opened his mouth wide and laughed so hard that his pince-nez nearly fell off. Naturally, I was offended, and demanded to know what was so funny. As I recall, Chuck's answer went roughly as follows. Though I may, of course, be mistaken about some of the details. After all, at that time I still did not fully understand the language of the kappa. “But surely it is absurd to consider nothing but the convenience of the parents. It really is far too selfish.” On the other hand, from our human point of view, there is truly nothing quite so ridiculous as childbirth among the kappa. Indeed, some time later I went to Bag's hut to watch his wife give birth. When the kappa give birth, matters are much the same as with us human beings. They too give birth with the assistance of doctors, midwives, and the like. But when the moment of birth arrives, the father puts his mouth to the mother's genitals as though making a telephone call and says, “Think carefully about whether you wish to be born into this world, and then give me your answer.” That is the question he asks in a loud voice.

p.src: “I do not wish to be born. To begin with, the madness I would inherit from my father is burden enough by itself. Besides, I believe that existence as a kappa is evil.” When Bag heard this answer, he scratched his head in embarrassment. The midwife in attendance, however, immediately thrust a thick glass tube into his wife's genitals and injected some sort of liquid. His wife then let out a deep breath of relief. At the same time, her belly, which until then had been so large, collapsed limply like a balloon emptied of hydrogen gas. Since they can give answers of this sort, kappa children can naturally walk and talk the moment they are born. According to Chuck, there was even a child who delivered a lecture on the existence or nonexistence of God on the twenty-sixth day after its birth. Though that child is said to have died in its second month. Since I have mentioned childbirth, let me tell you about a large poster I happened to see on a street corner in the third month after my arrival in this country. Along the bottom of this large poster were depicted a dozen or so kappa, some blowing trumpets and others holding swords. Above them, the entire surface was covered with the spiral script used by the kappa, which looked exactly like the mainspring of a clock. At any rate, I took down word for word in my notebook what a kappa student named Lap, who was walking with me, read aloud.

p.src: Of course, I told Lap that even then no such practice existed among us. At this, not only Lap but every kappa near the poster burst into loud laughter. “Doesn’t exist? Why, judging from what you have told us, I should think you people do the same thing we do. Why do you suppose young gentlemen fall in love with maids, and young ladies with chauffeurs? They are all unconsciously stamping out bad heredity. For one thing, compared with that volunteer corps of you humans which you told me about the other day—the volunteer corps whose members kill one another to seize a single railway—I should say our volunteer corps is far nobler.” Lap spoke with a solemn face, yet his great belly kept rippling as though it found the whole thing amusing. But far from laughing, I suddenly lunged to catch one of the kappas. For I had noticed that, taking advantage of my inattention, the kappa had stolen my fountain pen. But kappas, with their slippery skin, are not easily caught by us. No sooner had that kappa slipped smoothly from my grasp than he dashed away at full speed. He leaned his mosquito-thin body so far forward that he seemed about to topple over.
